description: Composite four-panel electron-microscopy figure (two ECCI micrographs plus two dark-field TEM images) showing the deformation structure and precipitation state of annealed Fe-30.5Mn-8.0Al-1.2C (8Al) steel; the group is mixed-modality. (a) ECCI of a short annealed 8Al sample tensile deformed to 0.3 true strain: bright and dark planar dislocation arrays crossing in two orientations to build a Taylor-lattice grid, with a 500 nm scale bar. (b) Dark-field TEM of the short annealed precipitation state (20 nm scale bar): heterogeneous, very fine bright precipitates on a dark matrix, with a selected-area diffraction inset (bottom right) of discrete spots. (c) ECCI of the long annealed 8Al steel after 0.15 true strain (500 nm scale bar); white arrows labelled "dislocation arrays" mark dense parallel boundaries in a mottled matrix. (d) Dark-field TEM of the long annealed 8Al sample (20 nm scale bar) resolving bright cuboidal precipitates separated by narrow matrix channels; white arrows mark sheared particles and a diffraction-pattern inset sits bottom right. The panels jointly argue that nanosized, shearable j-carbides promote planar slip, planar dislocation substructures and thus high strength with retained ductility.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an ECCI micrograph with a 500 nm scale bar in which bright, straight planar dislocation arrays cross at two distinct orientations forming a lattice-like (Taylor lattice) network.
Panel (c) contains five white arrows and the printed label "dislocation arrays", plus a 500 nm scale bar, marking dense parallel dislocation boundaries.
Panels (b) and (d) each carry a 20 nm scale bar and a diffraction-pattern inset in the bottom right corner; the inset spot positions cannot be indexed at the supplied resolution.

The precipitates appear visually different between the two dark-field images: (b) shows a fine, heterogeneous dot-like dispersion, whereas (d) shows coarser bright cuboidal particles arranged in rows with narrow dark matrix channels between them.
The caption states (a) is an ECCI image of Taylor lattice structures in a short annealed 8Al steel sample tensile deformed to 0.3 true strain.

The caption states (b) is a dark-field TEM image of the distribution of j-carbides in a short annealed 8Al sample, and (d) the same for a long annealed 8Al sample with sheared particles indicated by arrows.
The caption states (c) is an ECCI image of planar dislocation arrangements in a long annealed 8Al steel tensile deformed to 0.15 true strain, with dislocation arrays indicated by arrows.
The citing text states the short annealed 8Al steel develops Taylor lattice structures plus highly dense dislocation walls (HDDWs) spaced between 100 and 200 nm on the primary slip system.

The citing text states the short annealed precipitation distribution is heterogeneous with intragranular nanosized precipitates of 2-5 nm, identified by diffraction as j-carbides with a cube/cube orientation relationship with the austenite matrix.
The citing text states the long annealed 8Al steel contains a uniform distribution of intragranular cuboidal j-carbides with an average size of 10-20 nm and matrix channels about 2-3 nm wide.
The citing text states the long annealed 8Al steel deformed to 0.15 true strain forms planar dislocation substructures with dense dislocation arrays spaced between 100 and 300 nm.

The citing text reports yield strengths of 540 MPa (short annealed 8Al) and 990 MPa (long annealed 8Al) versus 420 MPa for the 2Al steel in solid solution, with UTS 1180 MPa and uniform elongation 37% for the long annealed 8Al.

No numeric data values, spacing labels or size numbers are printed as text inside any of the four panels; only scale bars (500 nm in a and c, 20 nm in b and d) and the words "dislocation arrays" are legible as annotations.

subfigures.description: ECCI micrograph of a short annealed 8Al steel deformed to 0.3 true strain, 500 nm scale bar. Bright and dark straight dislocation traces cross at two orientations to form a grid (Taylor lattice); some closely spaced parallel sheets form denser walls.

Dark-field TEM image, 20 nm scale bar, of the short annealed 8Al precipitation state: a heterogeneous dispersion of very fine bright particles on a dark background. A selected-area diffraction pattern inset (bottom right) shows discrete spots; the pattern is too small to index.

ECCI micrograph, 500 nm scale bar, of the long annealed 8Al steel deformed to 0.15 true strain. Five white arrows labelled "dislocation arrays" point at dense planar dislocation arrays running through a mottled background.

Dark-field TEM image, 20 nm scale bar, of the long annealed 8Al sample: bright cuboidal precipitates in rows separated by narrow dark matrix channels; three white arrows indicate sheared particles. A diffraction-pattern inset in the bottom right corner is unindexed at this resolution.
